chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said regarding the virgin woman, her permission is her silence, and the divorced/widow, her command is in her (control).

key_terms.أَمْرُهَا إِلَيْهَا: Her command/authority is in her own hands

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a virgin and a previously married woman regarding marriage consent in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from al-Kafi delineates the criteria for marital consent, establishing that a virgin’s (bikr) silence is legally interpreted as agreement, whereas a previously married woman (thayyib) must explicitly grant permission. This distinction reflects the juristic view that the experience of a thayyib necessitates active verbal consent to ensure her autonomy, while the bashfulness of a bikr is accommodated through tacit approval. The ruling underscores the balance between paternal authority and individual agency in Shia family law.
